---
title: "Palmer Penguins Dashboard: Matthew Emmanuel B. Albenio"
format: dashboard
theme: flatly
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Row {height=20%}

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Total Penguins"
list(icon = "binoculars", color = "primary", value = nrow(penguins))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Most Common Species"
list(icon = "award", color = "primary",
     value = names(which.max(table(penguins$species))))
```

```{r}
#| content: valuebox
#| title: "Island With The Most Penguins"
list(icon = "globe-americas", color = "primary",
     value = names(which.max(table(penguins$island))))
```

## Row {height=50%}

### Column

```{r}
#| title: "Penguins Species Distribution"
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = species, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Species", y = "Number of Penguins", fill = "Species") +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Column

```{r}
#| title: "Species Across Islands"
ggplot(penguins, aes(x = island, fill = species)) +
  geom_bar() +
  labs(x = "Island", y = "Number of Penguins", fill = "Species") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Row {height=30%}
::: {.card title="Interpretation"}
Adelie is the most frequently observed species with 152 penguins, followed by
Gentoo (124) and Chinstrap (68). Adelie makes up roughly 44% of all
observations, while Chinstrap makes up only about 20%.

Biscoe has the most penguins (168), followed by Dream (124) and Torgersen (52).
Adelie is the only species found on all three islands. Gentoo penguins live
only on Biscoe and Chinstrap penguins only on Dream, which explains why those
islands are so strongly tied to a single species.
:::
